dataset_role: Post-hoc diagnostic inspection of five previously observed queries, two unchanged index versions; not held-out, no model/solver calls.
method: Capture actual production Chroma semantic calls without changing arguments or returned values; all ten used k=16 and reproduce prior final record IDs.
Separately inspect raw Dense k=100 on the unchanged query. These are approximate HNSW ranks in that diagnostic call, not exact global vector ranks.

Observe BM25DocumentIndex.search return-frame scores with a process-local profiler, then sort by the existing (-score, chunk_id) order. Reconstructed page Top-20 equals the real method return in all ten calls.
Inspect predeclared target page/section bodies, excluding heading-only records. Targets are necessary evidence probes, not an exhaustive set of all valid answer passages.
Replay the page-selection loop over captured candidates and assert identical plain-Dense Top-4; distinguish actually skipped duplicates from candidates never scanned after the early stop.
Compare actual augmented returns with plain-Dense and inspect target excerpts only counterfactually. Do not count unreturned target text as delivered evidence.
Verify old/new index, implementation, source and previous artifact bindings before/after; no product code, index, prompt or default modified.

conclusions.finding: The targeted Scripting Reference OdbAssembly page has zero records in both general indices. None of the current Top-4 snippets answers member access. This is an entrypoint/source-coverage gap; changing same-page deduplication cannot create the absent reference.
conclusions.scope: Does not claim every possible document mentioning an ODB set is absent.

conclusions.finding: For the new Riks main query, Proportional Loading is raw Dense rank 6 and is actually skipped as a duplicate of the postbuckling page whose Incrementation chunk was selected at rank 3. The Riks Method body is rank 12 but the loop has already stopped after four unique pages. Its absence is not solely an embedding-recall failure.
conclusions.scope: Removing page deduplication alone while keeping raw Top-4 would still not return ranks 6 and 12; a candidate-level passage selection change must be tested.

conclusions.finding: For both Riks queries, plain Dense selects a STATIC Data line for the Riks method passage. The augmented path replaces it with the exact keyword overview from the same page. Thus the weakness is broader than AT: even a genuinely mentioned symbol can replace a more useful passage with a generic cover record.
conclusions.scope: Selection behavior confirmed; no Agent benefit or harm measured.

conclusions.finding: The Boundary Conditions body exists, but is absent from raw Dense Top-100 in both indices. Its complete BM25 score ranks are 697 old and 777 new, well outside a useful candidate budget. This is an upstream retrieval failure, not removal of an already-good Top-16 candidate.
conclusions.scope: The relative contributions of question wording, chunk representation and encoder limitations are not yet isolated. The targeted paragraph is evidence, not a complete answer to every aspect of the BC question.

conclusions.finding: For the second warning query, the main Standard exact-time increment-adjustment body is raw and page-deduplicated BM25 rank 1 in both indices. It is absent from the actual Dense Top-16; old diagnostic Dense Top-100 places it at 52, while new Top-100 does not contain it. This is a concrete observed BM25 complement to Dense.
conclusions.scope: One development query, not general Hybrid superiority; RRF was not executed in this audit.

conclusions.finding: For the first warning query, the main adjustment body is BM25 raw rank 14 old / 13 new. BM25 instead selects a same-page Time Points request-definition passage at raw rank 2; the adjustment explanation is discarded by page-level deduplication. BM25 page-hit is not a precise-section answer hit.
conclusions.scope: The second chunk of the target section ranks 9 old / 12 new, but chiefly contains performance consequences. It must not be counted as the complete increment-adjustment explanation solely by section title.

conclusions.finding: AT consumes rank 1 in both warning augmented queries. Direct plain-Dense Top-4 in this audit still lacks the exact-time target in both indices. Removing AT would remove an unrelated hit but is not sufficient to solve these warning queries.
conclusions.scope: No AT blacklist or routing change applied.

conclusions.finding: The main exact-time target contains procedure-specific minimum-increment exceptions in its full text. Its hypothetical 600-character return includes the beginning of the However exception clause in the old version, but truncates before that clause in the new version; neither delivers the entire exception list. Rich heading prefixes use body budget; even BM25 rank 1 would not deliver the entire qualified explanation through that formatter.
conclusions.scope: This is a return-format finding, not a claim that the unexecuted Agent actually received or misused it.

conclusions.finding: Actual cached MiniLM tokenizer measurements give 99-148 tokens for all five queries, below its 256-token truncation limit. All inspected body-bearing target records are also below 256 tokens. Query/target truncation at the embedding-tokenizer limit does not explain these selected failures.
conclusions.scope: Not an audit of every corpus record; 600-character output truncation is a separate layer.

next_step_recommendation_not_implemented: Test passage-level candidate selection before irreversible page deduplication, keeping sparse/dense candidates distinguishable and exact mentions non-authoritative. Separately verify a body-first evidence formatter. Do not assume removing AT, adding RRF or increasing K alone solves all needs; the BC query still needs upstream query/representation diagnosis and API members need their own coverage work.
